title: Supplementation with Low Doses of a Cod Protein Hydrolysate on Glucose Regulation and Lipid Metabolism in Adults with Metabolic Syndrome: A Randomized, Double-Blind Study

what_it_measured.text: Here, we investigated the effect of 8 weeks supplementation with 4 g of cod protein hydrolysate (CPH) on glucose metabolism, lipid profile and body composition in individuals with MetS in a double-blind, randomized intervention study with a parallel-group design.

dose.text: Here, we investigated the effect of 8 weeks supplementation with 4 g of cod protein hydrolysate (CPH) on glucose metabolism, lipid profile and body composition in individuals with MetS in a double-blind, randomized intervention study with a parallel-group design.
Participants with MetS received a daily supplement of 4 g of CPH (active ingredient) or placebo (no active ingredient) for 8 weeks.

endpoint.text: Secondary outcomes were fasting and postprandial insulin and glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1), fasting lipid concentrations and body composition.
Primary outcomes were serum fasting and postprandial glucose levels.
The primary outcome was fasting and postprandial glucose levels.

reported_results.text: The GLP-1 levels were on average 0.83 pmol/L higher (back transformed estimate) for participants who received CPH compared to placebo, but this was not significantly different (95% CI: (0.61, 1.13), p = 0.221).

The insulin levels were on average 0.63 mIU/L higher for CPH compared to placebo (95% CI: (−31.32, 32.58), p = 0.968), and we did not observe any changes in insulin levels from baseline visit to end of study in either of the groups (overall change: 0.57 mIU/L, 95% CI: (−4.79, 5.92), p = 0.836) (Figure 2c).

Glucose Homeostasis Adjusted for time and visit, the glucose levels were on average 0.55 mmol/L higher for CPH compared to placebo, but the linear mixed-effects model with repeated measures did not reveal any significant differences between the groups (95% CI: (−0.44, 1.53), p = 0.267).
Fasting TAG was reduced within the CPH group (mean diff: −0.81 mmol/L (back transformed estimate), 95% CI: (0.694, 0.948), p = 0.012), but did not differ from placebo (Figure 3).

At baseline, HbA1c was on average 37.5 ± 4.47 mmol/mol in the CPH group and 35.7 ± 3.40 mmol/mol in the placebo group, with no differences between groups (mean diff: 1.87, 95% CI: (−1.102, 4.835), p = 0.208).

numbers.text: Here, we investigated the effect of 8 weeks supplementation with 4 g of cod protein hydrolysate (CPH) on glucose metabolism, lipid profile and body composition in individuals with MetS in a double-blind, randomized intervention study with a parallel-group design.
Participants with MetS received a daily supplement of 4 g of CPH (active ingredient) or placebo (no active ingredient) for 8 weeks.
Secondary outcomes were fasting and postprandial insulin and glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1), fasting lipid concentrations and body composition.

The GLP-1 levels were on average 0.83 pmol/L higher (back transformed estimate) for participants who received CPH compared to placebo, but this was not significantly different (95% CI: (0.61, 1.13), p = 0.221).

The insulin levels were on average 0.63 mIU/L higher for CPH compared to placebo (95% CI: (−31.32, 32.58), p = 0.968), and we did not observe any changes in insulin levels from baseline visit to end of study in either of the groups (overall change: 0.57 mIU/L, 95% CI: (−4.79, 5.92), p = 0.836) (Figure 2c).

Glucose Homeostasis Adjusted for time and visit, the glucose levels were on average 0.55 mmol/L higher for CPH compared to placebo, but the linear mixed-effects model with repeated measures did not reveal any significant differences between the groups (95% CI: (−0.44, 1.53), p = 0.267).
Fasting TAG was reduced within the CPH group (mean diff: −0.81 mmol/L (back transformed estimate), 95% CI: (0.694, 0.948), p = 0.012), but did not differ from placebo (Figure 3).

At baseline, HbA1c was on average 37.5 ± 4.47 mmol/mol in the CPH group and 35.7 ± 3.40 mmol/mol in the placebo group, with no differences between groups (mean diff: 1.87, 95% CI: (−1.102, 4.835), p = 0.208).
